subject.title: diagnostics/memory: wire thresholds parameter to config (rssWarningBytes/rssCriticalBytes/heapUsedWarningBytes/heapUsedCriticalBytes)

question: Should gateway memory-pressure thresholds be operator-configurable, automatically derived from effective process/cgroup limits, or both under one documented diagnostics policy?
rationale: The reports establish real operator noise, but the repository policy sets a high bar for new config surfaces and the prior unmerged proposals disagree on contract scope.

options.title: Adopt a bounded optional threshold block
options.body: Expose only the RSS and heap warning/critical values with validation against effective defaults, retaining current behavior when absent.

options.title: Derive thresholds from resource limits
options.body: Use effective V8 and cgroup/service limits when available, avoiding a new operator-facing setting but requiring clear fallback semantics.

options.title: Defer until policy is settled
options.body: Keep the existing diagnostics behavior while documenting the intended threshold model before accepting another implementation.

recommendation.title: Adopt a bounded optional threshold block
recommendation.body: Expose only the RSS and heap warning/critical values with validation against effective defaults, retaining current behavior when absent.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the diagnostic runtime and public configuration schema boundary.
